edit.description: Generalize the hand-authored-lock home past guard fixtures. Three changes to `GuardLock` (:459). (1) Rename it for the job it does — a hand-rendered lock read back through the engine's own reader — since a session-start fixture is not a guard fixture; `LockFixture` unless a better name presents itself. (2) The mode becomes optional: `declaring(mode)` (:470) always pushes an `[[declaration.assembly]]` `mode` fact, and the four fixtures this entry routes declare none, so add a mode-less constructor and fire `write`'s (:540) mode assertion only where a mode was declared. (3) Widen the renderer with the families and columns those fixtures spell: the `requirement` and `satisfies` families (`Declarations::requirements`/`satisfies`, src/drift.rs:3714/:3721, rendered beside the existing four in `render` (:585) through `insert_declaration_family`), and the `bound`/`unit` columns on `clause_table` (:674). Every addition rides the same read-back backstop the existing families do — the rendered bytes must lift to exactly the declared rows.

Four raw `fs::write` lock fixtures route through the shared home: :149 (a `requirement` + `satisfies` pair standing in for a prior import), :191 (kind + clause with `bound`/`unit` + requirement + satisfies), :250 (kind + a `required` field clause), :300 (a lone unfilled `requirement`). Each is bytes today, so nothing checks that the spelling still matches `src/`: `family()` (src/drift.rs:4636) answers an empty vec for an absent family key, so a renamed `requirement` family makes the :149 fixture declare no requirement at all while its assertions — exit zero, no blocking verdict — stay green over a lock that demands nothing. That is the vacuity class `specs/process/engineering.md`, "A green verdict is proven non-vacuous" names, and the read-back is what closes it.
Rename ripple only: 6 `GuardLock` call sites follow the type's new name.

Rename ripple only: 13 `GuardLock` call sites follow the type's new name, including the fixture pin `a_guard_fixtures_lock_declares_its_enforcement_mode_rather_than_inheriting_the_default`, whose subject is now one constructor of two — it keeps asserting the declared mode row and the mode read back off it.

summary: The session-start suite hand-spells four lock fixtures as raw TOML; generalize the shared hand-lock home past guard fixtures and route them through its read-back.

tests.asserts: all four session-start lock fixtures declare their rows through the shared home, so each lock's bytes lift back to exactly the requirement/satisfies/kind/clause rows declared; renaming the `requirement` family in src/ turns the satisfies case red rather than leaving it green over an empty lock

acceptance: `cargo test` green, no `[[declaration.` text left in tests/it/session_start.rs, and the satisfies case red under a renamed `requirement` family in `src/`.
